artworks.title: Antigone Condemned to Death by Creon
artworks.description: Diotti's vast Accademia Carrara canvas stages the uncle-king at full authority: Creon sentences Antigone (and Ismene) while the court looks on. Thebes' rigid law made flesh — the decree that will wall the sister alive and ruin his own house.

artworks.title: Antigone Forced from Her Father
artworks.description: British Museum lithograph after Flaxman for Sophocles' Oedipus at Colonus: Creon seizes Antigone from the blind exile who clings to her. The Theban king as political force — reclaiming the daughters for Thebes against Athens' sanctuary.

artworks.title: Creon, King of Thebes (Costume Design)
artworks.description: BnF costume maquette labelled Creon roi de Thebes: the Theban king as a late-Ancien Régime stage figure in cloak and crown. Theatre's stock image of the uncle who holds the city after Oedipus falls.

artworks.title: Final Scene of Antigone: Creon Mourning Haemon
artworks.description: Nineteenth-century stage print of Sophocles' catastrophe: Creon (Bocage) weeps over Haemon's body while the Theban court gathers. The king who forbade burial learns too late what his decree cost — son, bride, and queen.

films.title: Antigone
films.description: Javellas' Creon is the law that will not bend — the uncle-king who walls Antigone alive and learns too late what the gods require.

films.title: Oedipus the King
films.description: Saville keeps Creon as the brother-in-law under suspicion — the future king already waiting in Sophocles' first Theban play.

music.title: Oedipus Rex
music.description: Stravinsky's Creon brings the Delphic word and the political edge — the brother of Jocasta as the state answering the plague.

music.title: Antigone
music.description: Honegger's Creon is the decree itself set to music — the king who forbids the burial and pays with his house.

popCulture.title: Antigone
popCulture.creator: Sophocles
popCulture.description: Sophocles' Creon forbids the burial and walls Antigone alive — the uncle-king whose decree becomes Western drama's type of rigid state law.

popCulture.title: Antigone
popCulture.creator: Jean Anouilh
popCulture.description: Anouilh's Creon argues like a collaborator-administrator — reasonable, exhausted, and still the man who will kill the girl for order.
